turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_te_zt900_train.csv: 300 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (O, Sb, Co, Si, Sn, Ca, Ni, Ti, Pb, Se, Ge, Cu, Zr, Te, S, Zn,
    Fe, Yb, Mn, Sr, Nb, Bi, Cd, Hf, In) and `target` (the measured zT
    (thermoelectric figure of merit) at 900 K).
  - b3_te_zt900_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose zT (thermoelectric
    figure of merit) at 900 K was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST zT
(thermoelectric figure of merit) at 900 K, then select the 5 best candidates
from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the training data

**1. Which chemistries dominate the high‑zT tail?**

Sorting the 300 training points, essentially all zT > 1.1 belong to a few families:

| family | typical training rows | zT |
|---|---|---|
| **PbTe (+S / Se / Sr)** | Pb 0.49/Te 0.35/S 0.15 → 2.21; Pb 0.32/Te 0.61/Se/Sr → 2.26; Pb/Te/Sr → 2.03–2.08 | **1.9 – 2.26** |
| **Cu₂Se (Cu:Se ≈ 2:1)** | Cu 0.637/Se 0.318 → 1.74; Cu 0.660/Se 0.330 → 1.45; Cu 0.667/Se 0.333 → 1.17 | 1.2 – 1.7 |
| **PbSe** | Pb 0.48/Se 0.50 → 1.40; Pb 0.475 → 1.24; Pb 0.465 → 1.19 (rises with Pb fraction) | 1.2 – 1.6 |
| **PbS(+Sn/Ca)** | Pb 0.49/S 0.50/Sn 0.01 → 1.04; +Ca → 1.08 | 0.7 – 1.1 |
| **Sn–Ni–Zr–Hf half‑Heusler (+trace Sb)** | Sb 0.003/Sn/Ni/Zr 0.13/Hf 0.19 → 1.35, 1.32 | 0.9 – 1.35 |
| Sb–Fe–Nb–Ti, Sb–Yb skutterudites, BiCuSeO | 0.6 – 1.14 | mid |

Oxides (O‑rich rows: SrTiO₃, ZnO, Ca‑Mn‑O, Co‑oxides), silicides and Si–Fe–Mn rows are almost all < 0.4 → discard all O‑containing pool entries.

**2. Applying this to the pool**

- **c052** — Pb 0.493 / Te 0.394 / S 0.099: nearest neighbour in training is Pb 0.494/Te 0.346/S 0.148 → **zT 2.21** (the PbTe–PbS alloy champion). Clear #1.
- **c054** — Cu 0.6515 / Se 0.3257: sits between the 1.45 and 1.74 Cu₂Se rows → ≈1.55–1.6.
- **c012** — Pb 0.500 / Se 0.498: the PbSe series increases monotonically with Pb content (1.19 → 1.24 → 1.40), and Sb‑doped PbSe reached 1.62 → extrapolate ≈1.5.
- **c063** — Cu 0.664 / Se 0.336, i.e. just off stoichiometric Cu₂Se → ≈1.2–1.3.
- **c097 / c025** — SnTe with tiny Mn / In (Sn 0.485, Te 0.50): training Sn 0.425/Te 0.50/Mn 0.075 gave 1.05, so ≈0.9–1.05 — better than the PbTe:Bi candidates (c001, c006, c041), whose training analogue (Pb 0.4925/Te 0.5/Bi 0.0075) only gave 0.68.
- Half‑Heusler candidates (c093, c073, c020, c078, c061, c031) lack the trace Sb that accompanies the 1.2–1.35 rows; their Sb‑free analogues fall to 0.4–0.9, so they rank just below.

**Final: c052, c054, c012, c063, c097**
